spanish-102.headline: Spanish 102 Core 30
spanish-102.threshold: Expand Spanish 101 through past narration, objects, plans, requests, commands and introductory subjunctive choices.

lessons.title: Two object pronouns
lessons.objective: Two object pronouns: Indirect precedes direct.

words.es: Se lo voy a devolver esta tarde.
words.en: I am going to return it to her this afternoon.
And the photos of her children?

words.es: También se las voy a llevar.
words.en: I am also going to take them to her.

words.es: Marta me prestó el libro el lunes.
words.en: Marta lent me the book on Monday.
I want to give it to her before the trip.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing returning a borrowed book. Indirect precedes direct. Le or les becomes se before lo, la, los or las; clarify the recipient when needed. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Pronouns with infinitives
lessons.objective: Pronouns with infinitives: With a conjugated verb plus infinitive, object pronouns can precede the conjugated verb or attach to the infinitive: lo voy a comprar / voy a comprarlo.

words.es: Voy a comprar un regalo para Luis.
words.en: I am going to buy a gift for Luis.

words.es: Lo voy a buscar en la tienda del centro.
words.en: I am going to look for it in the downtown store.
I prefer to buy it today.

words.es: Sí, te puedo acompañar después del trabajo.
words.en: Yes, I can go with you after work.

words.es: Queremos envolverlo antes de la fiesta.
words.en: We want to wrap it before the party.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing choosing a gift. With a conjugated verb plus infinitive, object pronouns can precede the conjugated verb or attach to the infinitive: lo voy a comprar / voy a comprarlo. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Gustar and similar verbs
lessons.objective: Gustar and similar verbs: The thing liked is the grammatical subject: me gusta el libro / me gustan los libros.

words.es: A mi amiga le interesa la historia.
words.en: My friend is interested in history.

words.es: Nos encanta conversar sobre los personajes.

words.en: Are you interested in our reading group?

words.es: Me gusta la idea, pero no me gustan las reuniones largas.
words.en: I like the idea, but I do not like long meetings.

words.es: Entonces te va a encantar nuestro horario.
words.en: Then you are going to love our schedule.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing joining a reading group. The thing liked is the grammatical subject: me gusta el libro / me gustan los libros. Interesar and encantar can follow the same pattern. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Reflexive and reciprocal meanings
lessons.objective: Reflexive and reciprocal meanings: Se can mean an action directed at oneself or, with a plural subject and context, a reciprocal action.

words.es: Nos encontramos en la plaza a las seis.
words.en: We met in the square at six.

words.es: Mis amigos se saludaron con un abrazo.
words.en: My friends greeted each other with a hug.

words.es: Después nos sentamos cerca de la fuente.
words.en: Then we sat down near the fountain.
We told each other the news.
When we said goodbye, we promised to see each other soon.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing meeting old friends. Se can mean an action directed at oneself or, with a plural subject and context, a reciprocal action. Clarify with el uno al otro when needed. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Accidental se
lessons.objective: Accidental se: Se me cayó presents an event as accidental; the affected person appears as me, te, le, nos or les.

words.es: Se me cayó una taza en la cocina.
words.en: I accidentally dropped a cup in the kitchen.

words.es: La taza se rompió en el suelo.
words.en: The cup broke on the floor.

words.es: A mi hermano se le olvidó traer una toalla.
words.en: My brother forgot to bring a towel.
We cleaned up the water carefully.

words.es: Por suerte nadie se hizo daño.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a broken cup. Se me cayó presents an event as accidental; the affected person appears as me, te, le, nos or les. The verb agrees with the thing: se me cayeron las llaves. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Comparatives and superlatives
lessons.objective: Comparatives and superlatives: Más / menos .

words.es: Este apartamento es más luminoso que el otro.
words.en: This apartment is brighter than the other one.

words.es: La cocina es menos grande, pero está mejor equipada.
words.en: The kitchen is smaller, but it is better equipped.

words.es: El alquiler es tan caro como el anterior.
words.en: The rent is as expensive as the previous one.

words.es: Este es el edificio más tranquilo de la calle.
words.en: This is the quietest building on the street.

words.es: Para mí, la ubicación es la mejor ventaja.
words.en: For me, the location is the best advantage.

words.es: Tenemos que comparar también los gastos.
words.en: We also need to compare the expenses.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing comparing apartments. Más / menos ... que compare; tan ... como states equality. Mejor and peor replace más bueno and más malo in ordinary comparisons; el más selects a group maximum. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Por and para with purpose
lessons.objective: Por and para with purpose: Para introduces a goal, recipient or deadline.

words.es: Este paquete es para mi hermana.
words.en: This package is for my sister.

words.es: Compré una caja para proteger el regalo.
words.en: I bought a box to protect the gift.

words.es: Pasé por la oficina de correos.
words.en: I went by the post office.

words.es: Pagué diez euros por el envío.
words.en: I paid ten euros for the shipping.

words.es: Gracias por ayudarme con la dirección.
words.en: Thank you for helping me with the address.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a package for a friend. Para introduces a goal, recipient or deadline. Por can give cause, route or exchange. Learn the relationship in context rather than translating both as for. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Relative clauses with que
lessons.objective: Relative clauses with que: Que connects a noun to identifying information: la persona que llamó.

words.es: Busco a la persona que organiza el curso.
words.en: I am looking for the person who organizes the course.

words.es: La mujer que está junto a la puerta es la coordinadora.
words.en: The woman who is next to the door is the coordinator.

words.es: Tengo una pregunta sobre el mensaje que recibí.
words.en: I have a question about the message I received.

words.es: El enlace que enviaron no funciona.
words.en: The link they sent does not work.

words.es: Ella me dio una dirección que sí funciona.
words.en: She gave me an address that does work.

words.es: Ahora puedo abrir el documento que necesito.
words.en: Now I can open the document I need.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing finding the right contact. Que connects a noun to identifying information: la persona que llamó. In Spanish que is retained where English sometimes omits that. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Negative and indefinite words
lessons.objective: Negative and indefinite words: Nadie, nada and nunca before the verb need no extra no; after the verb they normally pair with no.

words.es: No hay nadie en la oficina.
words.en: There is nobody in the office.
I did not find any new message.
Do you have any news from the director?
No, I still do not know anything.

words.es: Nunca cerramos tan temprano los lunes.
words.en: We never close this early on Mondays.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing an empty office. Nadie, nada and nunca before the verb need no extra no; after the verb they normally pair with no. Algún / ningún shorten before masculine singular nouns. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Quantity and agreement
lessons.objective: Quantity and agreement: Mucho, poco, demasiado and bastante can quantify nouns; most agree in gender and number, while bastante varies in number.

words.es: Hay demasiada sal en la sopa.
words.en: There is too much salt in the soup.
There are still quite a few tomatoes left.

words.es: Necesitamos mucha agua para la pasta.
words.en: We need a lot of water for the pasta.
We cooked quite a lot, but we ate little.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing preparing a class meal. Mucho, poco, demasiado and bastante can quantify nouns; most agree in gender and number, while bastante varies in number. Muy modifies adjectives and adverbs. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Future plans and predictions
lessons.objective: Future plans and predictions: The simple future adds endings to the infinitive, with irregular stems such as tendr- and har-.

words.es: El sábado visitaremos a nuestros primos.
words.en: On Saturday we will visit our cousins.

words.es: Vamos a salir temprano porque ya tenemos los boletos.
words.en: We are going to leave early because we already have the tickets.

words.es: Según el pronóstico, lloverá por la tarde.
words.en: According to the forecast, it will rain in the afternoon.
We will have to take umbrellas.
What will we do if they close the park?

words.es: Buscaremos un museo cerca del centro.
words.en: We will look for a museum near downtown.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a weekend forecast. The simple future adds endings to the infinitive, with irregular stems such as tendr- and har-. Ir a + infinitive often emphasizes an existing plan. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Conditional requests and advice
lessons.objective: Conditional requests and advice: The conditional uses infinitive or future irregular stem plus -ía endings.

words.es: Me gustaría quedarme una noche más.
words.en: I would like to stay one more night.
Would you have a quieter room?

words.es: Yo pediría una que no dé a la calle.
words.en: I would ask for one that does not face the street.

words.es: Sería mejor confirmar el precio primero.
words.en: It would be better to confirm the price first.

words.es: La recepcionista dijo que revisaría las opciones.
words.en: The receptionist said she would review the options.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing asking at reception. The conditional uses infinitive or future irregular stem plus -ía endings. It can soften requests and offer advice; politeness also depends on context and intonation. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Present perfect and experience
lessons.objective: Present perfect and experience: Haber in the present plus an invariant participle forms the present perfect.

words.es: Este mes he empezado un curso de cerámica.
words.en: This month I have started a pottery course.

words.es: Nunca he trabajado con este material.
words.en: I have never worked with this material.

words.es: Mi compañera ya ha hecho tres tazas.
words.en: My classmate has already made three cups.

words.es: Todavía no hemos terminado el primer proyecto.
words.en: We have not finished the first project yet.
Have you seen the workshop kiln?

words.es: Sí, pero aún no he abierto la puerta.
words.en: Yes, but I have not opened the door yet.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing trying a new activity. Haber in the present plus an invariant participle forms the present perfect. Regional preferences differ; many Latin American speakers use the preterite for events where Spain may use this perfect. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Irregular participles
lessons.objective: Irregular participles: With haber, participles stay unchanged: hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, abierto, puesto, vuelto and roto.

words.es: He abierto la sala de reuniones.
words.en: I have opened the meeting room.

words.es: Ana ha puesto las carpetas sobre la mesa.
words.en: Ana has put the folders on the table.

words.es: El director ha dicho que llegará a las diez.
words.en: The director has said that he will arrive at ten.
Have you seen the new document?

words.es: Sí, y hemos hecho una copia para cada persona.
words.en: Yes, and we have made a copy for each person.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a shared workspace. With haber, participles stay unchanged: hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, abierto, puesto, vuelto and roto. Do not agree them with the subject or object. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: The pluperfect
lessons.objective: The pluperfect: Imperfect haber plus an invariant participle places an event before another past reference: había salido cuando llamaste.

words.es: Cuando llegamos, la tienda ya había cerrado.
words.en: When we arrived, the store had already closed.

words.es: Yo había consultado un horario antiguo.
words.en: I had checked an old schedule.

words.es: Mi hermano había salido temprano del trabajo.
words.en: My brother had left work early.

words.es: Nadie nos había avisado del cambio.
words.en: Nobody had told us about the change.

words.es: Por suerte habíamos guardado el recibo.
words.en: Fortunately we had kept the receipt.

words.es: Volvimos al día siguiente para hacer el cambio.
words.en: We returned the next day to make the exchange.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing arriving after closing. Imperfect haber plus an invariant participle places an event before another past reference: había salido cuando llamaste. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Progressive aspect across time
lessons.objective: Progressive aspect across time: Estar plus a gerund highlights an action in progress.

words.en: Right now I am preparing a presentation.

words.es: Mis compañeros están leyendo los resultados.
words.en: My classmates are reading the results.

words.es: Ayer a esta hora estábamos buscando información.
words.en: Yesterday at this time we were looking for information.

words.es: Yo estaba escribiendo cuando se apagó la computadora.
words.en: I was writing when the computer turned off.

words.es: Hoy estamos guardando el trabajo con frecuencia.
words.en: Today we are saving the work frequently.

words.es: No estamos usando el equipo que falló ayer.
words.en: We are not using the equipment that failed yesterday.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a busy study room. Estar plus a gerund highlights an action in progress. Present estoy leyendo and imperfect estaba leyendo locate that action differently in time. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Affirmative tú commands
lessons.objective: Affirmative tú commands: Regular affirmative tú uses the él present form; common irregulars include di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven.

words.es: Ven a mi casa a las nueve.
words.en: Come to my house at nine.

words.es: Trae una caja pequeña si tienes.
words.en: Bring a small box if you have one.

words.es: Pon los libros junto a la puerta.
words.en: Put the books next to the door.

words.es: Haz una lista de las cosas frágiles.
words.en: Make a list of the fragile things.

words.es: Después llama a Julia y dile que ya estamos listos.
words.en: Then call Julia and tell her that we are ready.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing helping a friend move. Regular affirmative tú uses the él present form; common irregulars include di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven. Attached pronouns may require an accent. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Negative tú commands
lessons.objective: Negative tú commands: Negative tú uses no plus present subjunctive: no hables, no comas, no salgas.

words.es: No pongas esa olla en el borde.
words.en: Do not put that pot on the edge.

words.es: No uses el cuchillo que está roto.
words.en: Do not use the knife that is broken.
Do not mix the ingredients yet.

words.es: No lo dejes sobre la mesa mojada.
words.en: Do not leave it on the wet table.

words.es: No cierres la ventana, por favor.
words.en: Do not close the window, please.

words.es: No te preocupes; yo limpio al final.
words.en: Do not worry; I will clean up at the end.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing sharing a kitchen. Negative tú uses no plus present subjunctive: no hables, no comas, no salgas. Put object pronouns before the verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Formal commands
lessons.objective: Formal commands: Usted and ustedes commands use the corresponding present subjunctive.

words.es: Pase por esta puerta, por favor.
Deje la mochila en el casillero.
words.en: Leave your backpack in the locker.
Do not touch the works of art.

words.es: Si vienen en grupo, esperen junto a la escalera.
words.en: If you come as a group, wait next to the stairs.

words.es: Pregunten al personal si necesitan ayuda.
words.en: Ask the staff if you need help.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing directions at a museum. Usted and ustedes commands use the corresponding present subjunctive. No keeps the same form; compare pase and no pase. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Nosotros suggestions
lessons.objective: Nosotros suggestions: Vamos a + infinitive offers a plan; present-subjunctive nosotros can urge joint action: hablemos, comamos.

words.es: Primero hablemos de la fecha de entrega.
words.en: First let us talk about the deadline.

words.es: Escribamos las tareas en esta hoja.
words.en: Let us write the tasks on this sheet.

words.es: No dejemos todo para el último día.
words.en: Let us not leave everything until the last day.

words.es: Revisemos el borrador juntos el jueves.
words.en: Let us review the draft together on Thursday.

words.es: Terminemos la reunión y vámonos a clase.
words.en: Let us finish the meeting and go to class.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing organizing a group project. Vamos a + infinitive offers a plan; present-subjunctive nosotros can urge joint action: hablemos, comamos. Vámonos is a common irregular suggestion to leave. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Subjunctive for wishes
lessons.objective: Subjunctive for wishes: A wish such as quiero que with a new subject normally takes the subjunctive.

words.es: Quiero que mis padres conozcan la ciudad.
words.en: I want my parents to get to know the city.

words.es: Espero que el viaje sea tranquilo.
words.en: I hope the trip is peaceful.

words.es: Mi madre quiere visitar el mercado.
words.en: My mother wants to visit the market.

words.es: Mi padre prefiere que salgamos temprano.
words.en: My father prefers us to leave early.

words.es: Deseo que todos tengan tiempo para descansar.
words.en: I wish everyone had time to rest.

words.es: Yo quiero preparar una cena en casa.
words.en: I want to prepare dinner at home.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing planning a family visit. A wish such as quiero que with a new subject normally takes the subjunctive. With one subject, use an infinitive: quiero ir; quiero que vayas. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Subjunctive for emotion
lessons.objective: Subjunctive for emotion: Emotion about another subject often takes que plus subjunctive: me alegra que vengas.

words.es: Me alegra que vuelvas a clase.
words.en: I am glad you are coming back to class.

words.es: Nos sorprende que recuerdes tantos nombres.
words.en: We are surprised that you remember so many names.

words.es: A Laura le preocupa que el curso sea difícil.
words.en: Laura is worried that the course is difficult.

words.es: Me encanta que podamos estudiar juntos.
words.en: I love that we can study together.

words.es: Es una pena que Marcos no venga hoy.
words.en: It is a shame that Marcos is not coming today.

words.es: Espero que él pueda venir mañana.
words.en: I hope he can come tomorrow.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing welcoming a classmate back. Emotion about another subject often takes que plus subjunctive: me alegra que vengas. The emotion does not mean the event is false. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Subjunctive after doubt
lessons.objective: Subjunctive after doubt: Dudo que and no creo que commonly introduce subjunctive; creo que normally introduces indicative.

words.es: Creo que la biblioteca abre el sábado.
words.en: I think the library opens on Saturday.

words.es: No creo que cierre tan temprano.
words.en: I do not think it closes so early.

words.es: Dudo que ese anuncio sea reciente.
words.en: I doubt that that notice is recent.

words.es: Es posible que hayan cambiado el horario.
words.en: It is possible that they have changed the schedule.

words.es: Sabemos que el sitio web tiene un número de teléfono.
words.en: We know that the website has a phone number.
Let us call to confirm the information.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing checking a rumor. Dudo que and no creo que commonly introduce subjunctive; creo que normally introduces indicative. Choose the mood from the speaker's stance, not from que alone. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Subjunctive with recommendations
lessons.objective: Subjunctive with recommendations: Es importante que and recomiendo que take subjunctive for the advised action.

words.es: Es importante que llegues con tiempo.
words.en: It is important that you arrive with time to spare.

words.es: La profesora recomienda que practiquemos en parejas.
words.en: The teacher recommends that we practice in pairs.
It is advisable to review the instructions first.

words.es: Sugiero que grabes una respuesta corta.
words.en: I suggest that you record a short response.

words.es: Es mejor que no memorices un texto completo.
words.en: It is better if you do not memorize a complete text.

words.es: Quiero que puedas responder con tus propias palabras.
words.en: I want you to be able to answer in your own words.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing preparing for an oral exam. Es importante que and recomiendo que take subjunctive for the advised action. Use infinitive when no specific new subject is introduced. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Time clauses and future reference
lessons.objective: Time clauses and future reference: Cuando / en cuanto with a future or pending event usually take present subjunctive; habitual or established events take indicative.

words.es: Cuando llega un paquete, el portero nos llama.
words.en: When a package arrives, the doorman calls us.

words.es: Hoy estamos esperando una mesa nueva.
words.en: Today we are waiting for a new table.

words.es: Cuando llegue, voy a revisar la caja.
words.en: When it arrives, I am going to check the box.

words.es: En cuanto tengamos el recibo, te lo enviaré.
words.en: As soon as we have the receipt, I will send it to you.

words.es: No saldremos hasta que termine la entrega.
words.en: We will not leave until the delivery is finished.

words.es: Después de que revisemos todo, podremos salir.
words.en: After we check everything, we will be able to leave.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing waiting for a delivery. Cuando / en cuanto with a future or pending event usually take present subjunctive; habitual or established events take indicative. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Real conditions
lessons.objective: Real conditions: For an open condition about the future, si normally takes present indicative; the result may use future, present or a command.

words.es: Si hace buen tiempo, iremos al parque.
words.en: If the weather is good, we will go to the park.
If it rains, we will eat at home.
If you have a blanket, bring it.

words.es: Podemos comprar fruta si la tienda está abierta.
words.en: We can buy fruit if the store is open.

words.es: Si vienen tus primos, habrá comida suficiente.
words.en: If your cousins come, there will be enough food.

words.es: Te llamaré si cambia el plan.
words.en: I will call you if the plan changes.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a picnic with alternatives. For an open condition about the future, si normally takes present indicative; the result may use future, present or a command. Avoid future immediately after conditional si. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Hypothetical conditions

words.es: Buscaba mis llaves cuando ella llamó otra vez.
words.en: I was looking for my keys when she called again.

words.es: Abrí la puerta y le pedí un minuto.
words.en: I opened the door and asked her for a minute.

words.es: Mientras ella esperaba, encontré las llaves.
words.en: While she was waiting, I found the keys.
We left together for the station.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing finding and encountering. Encontrar changes o to ue in stressed present forms. Encontrarse can describe meeting someone or a person's condition, depending on context. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Putting inside
lessons.objective: Putting inside: Meter emphasizes putting inside; meter en introduces the container.

words.en: Do you have the hotel reservation?

words.es: Sí, la tengo en el teléfono.
words.en: Yes, I have it on my phone.
Where did you put the tickets?

words.es: Los puse dentro de la mochila.
words.en: I put them inside the backpack.

words.es: Necesito el pasaporte, pero no lo encuentro.
words.en: I need the passport, but I cannot find it.

words.es: Aquí está; lo dejaste sobre la mesa.
words.en: Here it is; you left it on the table.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing putting inside. Meter emphasizes putting inside; meter en introduces the container. Meterse en can describe entering or getting involved. It is a regular -er verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Starting an activity
lessons.objective: Starting an activity: Empezar a + infinitive introduces the activity begun.

words.es: Busqué una mesa cerca de la ventana.
words.en: I looked for a table near the window.
I began to read the menu.

words.es: Almorcé con una amiga del trabajo.
words.en: I had lunch with a friend from work.
I paid the bill by card.

words.es: Saqué el recibo de mi bolso.
words.en: I took the receipt out of my bag.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing starting an activity. Empezar a + infinitive introduces the activity begun. Present empiezo changes e to ie; preterite empecé changes z to c in yo. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Knowing and meeting
lessons.objective: Knowing and meeting: Conocer takes a personal a for specific people.

words.en: I have lived here since January.

words.es: Trabajo en la biblioteca desde hace dos meses.
words.en: I have worked at the library for two months.

words.es: Hace tres semanas conocí a mis vecinos.
words.en: I met my neighbors three weeks ago.

words.es: No veo a mi hermano desde el verano.
words.en: I have not seen my brother since the summer.
How long have you been studying Spanish?

words.es: Estudio español desde el año pasado.
words.en: I have been studying Spanish since last year.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing knowing and meeting. Conocer takes a personal a for specific people. Conocí a alguien often describes meeting for the first time. Contrast saber for information or skills. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Ability, possibility and permission
lessons.objective: Ability, possibility and permission: Poder + infinitive describes ability or possibility.

words.es: Me gustaría quedarme una noche más.
words.en: I would like to stay one more night.
Would you have a quieter room?

words.es: Yo pediría una que no dé a la calle.
words.en: I would ask for one that does not face the street.

words.es: Sería mejor confirmar el precio primero.
words.en: It would be better to confirm the price first.

words.es: La recepcionista dijo que revisaría las opciones.
words.en: The receptionist said she would review the options.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing ability, possibility and permission. Poder + infinitive describes ability or possibility. Puedo changes o to ue; pude uses a strong preterite stem; podría can soften a request. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Looking with attention
lessons.objective: Looking with attention: Mirar directs attention; ver describes seeing or watching in many contexts.

words.es: Este apartamento es más luminoso que el otro.
words.en: This apartment is brighter than the other one.

words.es: La cocina es menos grande, pero está mejor equipada.
words.en: The kitchen is smaller, but it is better equipped.

words.es: El alquiler es tan caro como el anterior.
words.en: The rent is as expensive as the previous one.

words.es: Este es el edificio más tranquilo de la calle.
words.en: This is the quietest building on the street.

words.es: Para mí, la ubicación es la mejor ventaja.
words.en: For me, the location is the best advantage.

words.es: Tenemos que comparar también los gastos.
words.en: We also need to compare the expenses.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing looking with attention. Mirar directs attention; ver describes seeing or watching in many contexts. Mirar is regular and often takes a direct object without a preposition. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Asking for something
lessons.objective: Asking for something: Pedir asks for something; preguntar asks a question.

words.es: Mi primo pidió una habitación tranquila.
words.en: My cousin asked for a quiet room.

words.es: La recepcionista repitió el número del piso.
words.en: The receptionist repeated the floor number.

words.es: Mi primo durmió hasta las nueve.
Sus hijos durmieron un poco más.
words.en: His children slept a little longer.

words.es: Por la mañana todos pidieron agua.
words.en: In the morning everyone asked for water.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing asking for something. Pedir asks for something; preguntar asks a question. Present pido changes e to i; preterite pidió and pidieron change in the third persons only. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Understanding a message
lessons.objective: Understanding a message: Entender changes e to ie in stressed present forms: entiendo, entiendes; entendemos keeps e.

words.es: Le escribí a Rosa esta mañana.
words.en: I wrote to Rosa this morning.

words.es: Le expliqué el cambio de horario.
words.en: I explained the schedule change to her.

words.es: Nos mandó la dirección del nuevo local.
words.en: She sent us the address of the new venue.
Did you let the others know?

words.es: Sí, les envié un mensaje a todos.
words.en: Yes, I sent a message to all of them.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing understanding a message. Entender changes e to ie in stressed present forms: entiendo, entiendes; entendemos keeps e. Use no entendí for a completed failure to understand. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Living and experiences
lessons.objective: Living and experiences: Vivir en names a residence; vivir una experiencia describes experiencing it.

words.en: We used to live near the river.

words.es: Nuestra casa tenía un patio pequeño.
words.en: Our house had a small courtyard.
My grandmother looked after the plants.

words.es: Yo iba a la escuela a pie.
words.en: I used to walk to school.

words.es: Desde la ventana veíamos las montañas.
words.en: From the window we could see the mountains.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing living and experiences. Vivir en names a residence; vivir una experiencia describes experiencing it. It is a regular -ir model, useful for present, preterite and imperfect contrasts. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

spanish-conjugation-patterns.headline: Spanish Conjugation Patterns Core 30
spanish-conjugation-patterns.threshold: Practice 28 named teaching patterns across 60 lessons, with ten distinct verbs and checked forms in every lesson.

lessons.title: Regular -ar preterite
lessons.objective: Regular -ar preterite: Completed bounded events use -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron.

words.es: Ayer llegué tarde a la estación.
words.en: Yesterday I arrived late at the station.
First I looked for the correct exit.
Then I bought a one-way ticket.

words.es: El tren salió a las ocho.
Llamé a Elena y expliqué el problema.
words.en: I called Elena and explained the problem.
In the end we took a bus.

lessons.speaking: Use Regular -ar preterite while discussing a late arrival. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a late arrival. Completed bounded events use -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron. Yo and él forms require written accents; nosotros matches present in spelling. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Regular -er / -ir preterite
lessons.objective: Regular -er / -ir preterite: Use -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron.

words.en: I normally used to have breakfast at home.

words.es: El lunes desayuné en la estación.
words.en: On Monday I had breakfast at the station.

words.es: Siempre llevaba un libro en la mochila.
words.en: I always used to carry a book in my backpack.
That day I forgot the backpack.

words.es: Mientras esperaba el tren, compré un periódico.
words.en: While I was waiting for the train, I bought a newspaper.

words.es: El viaje fue distinto de lo habitual.
words.en: The journey was different from the usual one.

lessons.speaking: Use Regular -er / -ir preterite while discussing a changed routine. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a changed routine. Use -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron. This bank avoids vowel-stem and other irregular preterites. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Preterite spelling changes
lessons.objective: Preterite spelling changes: In yo, -car becomes -qué, -gar becomes -gué, and -zar becomes -cé to preserve pronunciation.

words.es: Busqué una mesa cerca de la ventana.
words.en: I looked for a table near the window.
I began to read the menu.

words.es: Almorcé con una amiga del trabajo.
words.en: I had lunch with a friend from work.
I paid the bill by card.

words.es: Saqué el recibo de mi bolso.
words.en: I took the receipt out of my bag.

lessons.speaking: Use Preterite spelling changes while discussing paying for lunch. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing paying for lunch. In yo, -car becomes -qué, -gar becomes -gué, and -zar becomes -cé to preserve pronunciation. Other persons follow regular -ar endings. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Strong irregular preterite
lessons.objective: Strong irregular preterite: Use the memorized irregular stem with -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron, without written accents.

words.es: Tuve una cita en el centro.
El autobús estuvo lleno toda la mañana.
words.en: The bus was full all morning.
I could not get there on time.

words.es: La recepcionista puso mi nombre en otra lista.
words.en: The receptionist put my name on another list.

words.es: Hice una llamada desde la entrada.
words.en: I made a call from the entrance.

words.es: Al final el médico hizo espacio en su horario.
words.en: In the end the doctor made room in his schedule.

lessons.speaking: Use Strong irregular preterite while discussing a difficult appointment. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a difficult appointment. Use the memorized irregular stem with -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -ieron, without written accents. Decir uses dijeron; hacer uses hizo. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Preterite -ir stem changes
lessons.objective: Preterite -ir stem changes: These -ir verbs change e to i or o to u only in él / ella / usted and ellos / ellas / ustedes.

words.es: Mi primo pidió una habitación tranquila.
words.en: My cousin asked for a quiet room.

words.es: La recepcionista repitió el número del piso.
words.en: The receptionist repeated the floor number.

words.es: Mi primo durmió hasta las nueve.
Sus hijos durmieron un poco más.
words.en: His children slept a little longer.

words.es: Por la mañana todos pidieron agua.
words.en: In the morning everyone asked for water.

lessons.speaking: Use Preterite -ir stem changes while discussing an overnight visit. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing an overnight visit. These -ir verbs change e to i or o to u only in él / ella / usted and ellos / ellas / ustedes. Nosotros keeps the infinitive stem. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Past habits: -ar imperfect
lessons.objective: Past habits: -ar imperfect: Use -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban for background, ongoing situations and habitual past actions.

words.en: We used to live near the river.

words.es: Nuestra casa tenía un patio pequeño.
words.en: Our house had a small courtyard.
My grandmother looked after the plants.

words.es: Yo iba a la escuela a pie.
words.en: I used to walk to school.

words.es: Desde la ventana veíamos las montañas.
words.en: From the window we could see the mountains.

lessons.speaking: Use Past habits: -ar imperfect while discussing the old neighborhood. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing the old neighborhood. Use -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban for background, ongoing situations and habitual past actions. Context separates yo from él. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Past habits: -er / -ir imperfect
lessons.objective: Past habits: -er / -ir imperfect: Use -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían for background and repeated past actions.

words.en: I normally used to have breakfast at home.

words.es: El lunes desayuné en la estación.
words.en: On Monday I had breakfast at the station.

words.es: Siempre llevaba un libro en la mochila.
words.en: I always used to carry a book in my backpack.
That day I forgot the backpack.

words.es: Mientras esperaba el tren, compré un periódico.
words.en: While I was waiting for the train, I bought a newspaper.

words.es: El viaje fue distinto de lo habitual.
words.en: The journey was different from the usual one.

lessons.speaking: Use Past habits: -er / -ir imperfect while discussing a changed routine. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a changed routine. Use -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían for background and repeated past actions. All these endings carry a written accent. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Future simple
lessons.objective: Future simple: Add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án to the infinitive or listed irregular future stem.

words.es: El sábado visitaremos a nuestros primos.
words.en: On Saturday we will visit our cousins.

words.es: Vamos a salir temprano porque ya tenemos los boletos.
words.en: We are going to leave early because we already have the tickets.

words.es: Según el pronóstico, lloverá por la tarde.
words.en: According to the forecast, it will rain in the afternoon.
We will have to take umbrellas.
What will we do if they close the park?

words.es: Buscaremos un museo cerca del centro.
words.en: We will look for a museum near downtown.

lessons.speaking: Use Future simple while discussing a weekend forecast. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a weekend forecast. Add -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án to the infinitive or listed irregular future stem. The future can predict and can express a guess. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Conditional simple
lessons.objective: Conditional simple: Add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to the infinitive or irregular future stem.

words.es: Me gustaría quedarme una noche más.
words.en: I would like to stay one more night.
Would you have a quieter room?

words.es: Yo pediría una que no dé a la calle.
words.en: I would ask for one that does not face the street.

words.es: Sería mejor confirmar el precio primero.
words.en: It would be better to confirm the price first.

words.es: La recepcionista dijo que revisaría las opciones.
words.en: The receptionist said she would review the options.

lessons.speaking: Use Conditional simple while discussing asking at reception. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing asking at reception. Add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían to the infinitive or irregular future stem. Use for hypothetical results and softened requests. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Present subjunctive
lessons.objective: Present subjunctive: After a suitable trigger such as Espero que, use the present subjunctive.

words.es: Quiero que mis padres conozcan la ciudad.
words.en: I want my parents to get to know the city.

words.es: Espero que el viaje sea tranquilo.
words.en: I hope the trip is peaceful.

words.es: Mi madre quiere visitar el mercado.
words.en: My mother wants to visit the market.

words.es: Mi padre prefiere que salgamos temprano.
words.en: My father prefers us to leave early.

words.es: Deseo que todos tengan tiempo para descansar.
words.en: I wish everyone had time to rest.

words.es: Yo quiero preparar una cena en casa.
words.en: I want to prepare dinner at home.

lessons.speaking: Use Present subjunctive while discussing planning a family visit. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing planning a family visit. After a suitable trigger such as Espero que, use the present subjunctive. Start from yo present, remove o, and switch ar to e endings, er/ir to a endings; learn exceptions. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Imperfect subjunctive: -ra
lessons.objective: Imperfect subjunctive: -ra: Take the preterite ellos form, remove -ron, and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran; accent the nosotros stem vowel.

words.es: Si tuviera más tiempo, aprendería a tocar el piano.
words.en: If I had more time, I would learn to play the piano.

words.es: Si viviera cerca, iría a clase a pie.
words.en: If I lived nearby, I would walk to class.
My sister would come if she could.

words.es: ¿Qué harías si no trabajaras los viernes?
words.en: What would you do if you did not work on Fridays?

words.es: Yo visitaría a mi familia más seguido.
words.en: I would visit my family more often.

words.es: Si organizáramos mejor la semana, descansaríamos más.
words.en: If we organized the week better, we would rest more.

lessons.speaking: Use Imperfect subjunctive: -ra while discussing imagining a different schedule. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing imagining a different schedule. Take the preterite ellos form, remove -ron, and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -ran; accent the nosotros stem vowel. Used after past wishes and in si hypotheses. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Affirmative tú commands
lessons.objective: Affirmative tú commands: For regular affirmative tú commands use the él present form.

words.es: Ven a mi casa a las nueve.
words.en: Come to my house at nine.

words.es: Trae una caja pequeña si tienes.
words.en: Bring a small box if you have one.

words.es: Pon los libros junto a la puerta.
words.en: Put the books next to the door.

words.es: Haz una lista de las cosas frágiles.
words.en: Make a list of the fragile things.

words.es: Después llama a Julia y dile que ya estamos listos.
words.en: Then call Julia and tell her that we are ready.

lessons.speaking: Use Affirmative tú commands while discussing helping a friend move. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing helping a friend move. For regular affirmative tú commands use the él present form. Memorize di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven; this bank practices those eight plus two regular verbs. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Negative tú commands
lessons.objective: Negative tú commands: Use no plus the tú present subjunctive.

words.es: No pongas esa olla en el borde.
words.en: Do not put that pot on the edge.

words.es: No uses el cuchillo que está roto.
words.en: Do not use the knife that is broken.
Do not mix the ingredients yet.

words.es: No lo dejes sobre la mesa mojada.
words.en: Do not leave it on the wet table.

words.es: No cierres la ventana, por favor.
words.en: Do not close the window, please.

words.es: No te preocupes; yo limpio al final.
words.en: Do not worry; I will clean up at the end.

lessons.speaking: Use Negative tú commands while discussing sharing a kitchen. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing sharing a kitchen. Use no plus the tú present subjunctive. Affirmative and negative tú commands use different patterns. Any object pronoun goes before the verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Usted / ustedes commands
lessons.objective: Usted / ustedes commands: Use the usted or ustedes present subjunctive for formal commands.

words.es: Pase por esta puerta, por favor.
Deje la mochila en el casillero.
words.en: Leave your backpack in the locker.
Do not touch the works of art.

words.es: Si vienen en grupo, esperen junto a la escalera.
words.en: If you come as a group, wait next to the stairs.

words.es: Pregunten al personal si necesitan ayuda.
words.en: Ask the staff if you need help.

lessons.speaking: Use Usted / ustedes commands while discussing directions at a museum. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing directions at a museum. Use the usted or ustedes present subjunctive for formal commands. No creates a negative command with the same verb form. Both addressees are practiced. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Present progressive
lessons.objective: Present progressive: Use estar plus -ando for -ar or -iendo for -er/-ir to emphasize an action in progress.

words.en: Right now I am preparing a presentation.

words.es: Mis compañeros están leyendo los resultados.
words.en: My classmates are reading the results.

words.es: Ayer a esta hora estábamos buscando información.
words.en: Yesterday at this time we were looking for information.

words.es: Yo estaba escribiendo cuando se apagó la computadora.
words.en: I was writing when the computer turned off.

words.es: Hoy estamos guardando el trabajo con frecuencia.
words.en: Today we are saving the work frequently.

words.es: No estamos usando el equipo que falló ayer.
words.en: We are not using the equipment that failed yesterday.

lessons.speaking: Use Present progressive while discussing a busy study room. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a busy study room. Use estar plus -ando for -ar or -iendo for -er/-ir to emphasize an action in progress. Leer uses leyendo; dormir uses durmiendo; pedir uses pidiendo. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Present perfect
lessons.objective: Present perfect: Use he, has, ha, hemos, han plus an invariant participle.

words.es: Este mes he empezado un curso de cerámica.
words.en: This month I have started a pottery course.

words.es: Nunca he trabajado con este material.
words.en: I have never worked with this material.

words.es: Mi compañera ya ha hecho tres tazas.
words.en: My classmate has already made three cups.

words.es: Todavía no hemos terminado el primer proyecto.
words.en: We have not finished the first project yet.
Have you seen the workshop kiln?

words.es: Sí, pero aún no he abierto la puerta.
words.en: Yes, but I have not opened the door yet.

lessons.speaking: Use Present perfect while discussing trying a new activity. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing trying a new activity. Use he, has, ha, hemos, han plus an invariant participle. Regular participles end in -ado or -ido; learn the listed irregular ones. Regional use versus the preterite varies. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Pluperfect: earlier past
lessons.objective: Pluperfect: earlier past: Use había, habías, había, habíamos, habían plus an invariant participle for an action already completed before another past reference point.

words.es: Cuando llegamos, la tienda ya había cerrado.
words.en: When we arrived, the store had already closed.

words.es: Yo había consultado un horario antiguo.
words.en: I had checked an old schedule.

words.es: Mi hermano había salido temprano del trabajo.
words.en: My brother had left work early.

words.es: Nadie nos había avisado del cambio.
words.en: Nobody had told us about the change.

words.es: Por suerte habíamos guardado el recibo.
words.en: Fortunately we had kept the receipt.

words.es: Volvimos al día siguiente para hacer el cambio.
words.en: We returned the next day to make the exchange.

lessons.speaking: Use Pluperfect: earlier past while discussing arriving after closing. You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing arriving after closing. Use había, habías, había, habíamos, habían plus an invariant participle for an action already completed before another past reference point. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details.
