Conocí a can describe meeting for the first time. Present yo is conozco. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 22. crear · Making something new
lessons.objective: 22. crear · Making something new: Crear is regular and means create, not believe.

words.es: Creo una carpeta para cada proyecto.
words.en: I create a folder for each project.

words.es: Ana creó una lista con todos los contactos.
words.en: Ana created a list with all the contacts.

words.es: Estamos creando una guía para los visitantes.
words.en: We are creating a guide for visitors.

words.es: ¿Podemos crear una copia sin los datos privados?
words.en: Can we create a copy without the private details?

words.es: La directora quiere que creemos un ejemplo sencillo.
words.en: The director wants us to create a simple example.

words.es: Después lo probaremos con el grupo nuevo.
words.en: Afterward we will test it with the new group.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing making something new. Crear is regular and means create, not believe. Creer means believe; compare creo una lista with creo que la lista está lista. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 23. presentar · Presenting, introducing and submitting
lessons.objective: 23. presentar · Presenting, introducing and submitting: Presentar can introduce a person, present an idea or submit a document.

words.es: Presento el plan al comienzo de la reunión.
words.en: I present the plan at the beginning of the meeting.

words.es: Ana me presentó a su nueva compañera.
words.en: Ana introduced me to her new coworker.

words.es: Ayer presentamos la solicitud antes del plazo.
words.en: Yesterday we submitted the application before the deadline.
Who is going to present the results?

words.es: Quiero que cada persona se presente brevemente.
words.en: I want each person to introduce themselves briefly.

words.es: Así sabremos quién puede ayudar con cada tarea.
words.en: That way we will know who can help with each task.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing presenting, introducing and submitting. Presentar can introduce a person, present an idea or submit a document. Presentarse can introduce oneself or appear, depending on context. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 24. permitir · Allowing an action
lessons.objective: 24. permitir · Allowing an action: Permitir + infinitive can name an allowed activity; permitir que + subjunctive introduces an allowed action by a subject.

words.es: La tarjeta permite entrar al edificio.
words.en: The card allows entry to the building.

words.es: La coordinadora permite que usemos la sala por la tarde.
words.en: The coordinator allows us to use the room in the afternoon.

words.es: Ayer no permitieron abrir la puerta lateral.
words.en: Yesterday they did not allow the side door to be opened.

words.es: ¿Permiten guardar materiales aquí durante la noche?
words.en: Do they allow materials to be stored here overnight?

words.es: El nuevo horario nos permitirá trabajar con más calma.
words.en: The new schedule will allow us to work more calmly.

words.es: Antes de decidir, debemos revisar las condiciones.
words.en: Before deciding, we should review the conditions.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing allowing an action. Permitir + infinitive can name an allowed activity; permitir que + subjunctive introduces an allowed action by a subject. It is a regular -ir verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 25. dejar · Leaving, allowing and stopping
lessons.objective: 25. dejar · Leaving, allowing and stopping: Dejar algo leaves an item; dejar + infinitive can allow an action; dejar de + infinitive stops an activity.

words.en: I leave a copy at reception.

words.es: Ana me dejó usar su computadora.
words.en: Ana let me use her computer.

words.es: Ayer dejamos de trabajar a las seis.
words.en: Yesterday we stopped working at six.

words.es: No dejes los documentos junto a la ventana abierta.
words.en: Do not leave the documents next to the open window.
Can you let me review the last page?

words.es: Después se la enviaré a la coordinadora.
words.en: Afterward I will send it to the coordinator.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing leaving, allowing and stopping. Dejar algo leaves an item; dejar + infinitive can allow an action; dejar de + infinitive stops an activity. Keep the construction and meaning together. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 26. tratar · Attempts, topics and treatment
lessons.objective: 26. tratar · Attempts, topics and treatment: Tratar de + infinitive means try to; tratar de un tema concerns a subject; tratar a alguien describes treatment of a person.

words.es: Trato de resolver el problema antes del viernes.
words.en: I am trying to solve the problem before Friday.

words.es: La reunión trata de los horarios nuevos.
words.en: The meeting concerns the new schedules.

words.es: La recepcionista nos trata con mucha paciencia.
words.en: The receptionist treats us with great patience.

words.es: Ayer tratamos de llamar dos veces.
words.en: Yesterday we tried to call twice.

words.es: No trates de cambiar todos los datos a la vez.
words.en: Do not try to change all the details at once.

words.es: Primero confirmemos cuál es el error.
words.en: First let us confirm what the error is.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing attempts, topics and treatment. Tratar de + infinitive means try to; tratar de un tema concerns a subject; tratar a alguien describes treatment of a person. The complements determine the sense. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 27. parecer · Impressions and resemblance
lessons.objective: 27. parecer · Impressions and resemblance: Parecer offers an impression; parecerse a expresses resemblance.

words.es: Me parece que falta una fecha.
words.en: It seems to me that a date is missing.

words.es: Ayer parecía que todo estaba confirmado.
words.en: Yesterday it seemed that everything was confirmed.

words.es: ¿Te parece bien preguntar antes de enviar la copia?
words.en: Does it seem all right to you to ask before sending the copy?

words.es: Esta sala se parece a la que usamos antes.
words.en: This room resembles the one we used before.

words.es: Vamos a comparar los planos para estar seguros.
words.en: Let us compare the plans to be sure.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing impressions and resemblance. Parecer offers an impression; parecerse a expresses resemblance. Present yo is parezco. Parece que normally takes indicative when reporting an impression. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 28. ofrecer · Making an offer
lessons.objective: 28. ofrecer · Making an offer: Ofrecer uses ofrezco in present yo.

words.es: Ofrezco mi ayuda para preparar la sala.
words.en: I offer my help to prepare the room.

words.es: El centro ofrece clases por la tarde.
words.en: The center offers classes in the afternoon.
Ana offered to send the documents.
Could you offer us another date?

words.es: Mi compañero se ofreció a llamar a los participantes.
words.en: My coworker volunteered to call the participants.

words.es: Así podremos avisar a todos a tiempo.
words.en: That way we will be able to notify everyone in time.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing making an offer. Ofrecer uses ofrezco in present yo. Ofrecer algo a alguien names an offer; ofrecerse a + infinitive volunteers an action. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 29. contar · Numbers, stories and available support
lessons.objective: 29. contar · Numbers, stories and available support: Contar can count, tell a story or report something; contar con means have available or rely on.
lessons.focus: 29. contar · Numbers, stories and available support

words.es: Cuento las sillas antes de abrir la sala.
words.en: I count the chairs before opening the room.

words.es: Ana nos contó cómo había cambiado el horario.
words.en: Ana told us how the schedule had changed.

words.es: Contamos con dos personas para recibir a los visitantes.
words.en: We have two people available to welcome the visitors.
Can you tell me what happened yesterday?

words.es: Si contamos las copias ahora, evitaremos un problema después.
words.en: If we count the copies now, we will avoid a problem later.

words.es: No quiero que nadie se quede sin material.
words.en: I do not want anyone to be left without material.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing numbers, stories and available support. Contar can count, tell a story or report something; contar con means have available or rely on. Present cuento changes o to ue, but contamos keeps o. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 30. quedar · What remains and what was agreed
lessons.objective: 30. quedar · What remains and what was agreed: Quedar can mean remain, be situated or arrange a meeting.
lessons.focus: 30. quedar · What remains and what was agreed

words.es: Quedan tres lugares libres en el grupo.
words.en: There are three places left in the group.

words.es: La oficina queda cerca de la estación.
words.en: The office is near the station.

words.es: Quedamos en llamar después del almuerzo.
words.en: We agreed to call after lunch.

words.es: ¿A qué hora quedaste con la coordinadora?
words.en: What time did you arrange to meet the coordinator?

words.es: Yo me quedaré aquí hasta que termine la revisión.
words.en: I will stay here until the review is finished.

words.es: Después podremos salir juntos hacia la parada.
words.en: Afterward we will be able to leave together for the stop.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing what remains and what was agreed. Quedar can mean remain, be situated or arrange a meeting. Quedar en + infinitive records an agreement; quedarse can mean stay. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 31. utilizar · Using a resource for a purpose
lessons.objective: 31. utilizar · Using a resource for a purpose: Utilizar is regular except spelling changes such as utilicé / utilice.
lessons.focus: 31. utilizar · Using a resource for a purpose

words.es: Utilizo una lista para comprobar los nombres.
words.en: I use a list to check the names.

words.es: Ana utilizó el mapa que nos mandaron.
words.en: Ana used the map they sent us.

words.es: No utilizamos la sala pequeña porque estaba ocupada.
words.en: We did not use the small room because it was occupied.

words.es: ¿Podemos utilizar estas mesas para el taller?
words.en: Can we use these tables for the workshop?

words.es: La coordinadora pidió que utilizáramos solo la versión nueva.
words.en: The coordinator asked us to use only the new version.

words.es: Así todos tendremos las mismas instrucciones.
words.en: That way we will all have the same instructions.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing using a resource for a purpose. Utilizar is regular except spelling changes such as utilicé / utilice. It means use and often takes para + infinitive for the purpose. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 32. conseguir · Obtaining a result
lessons.objective: 32. conseguir · Obtaining a result: Conseguir uses consigo / consigues in the present and consiguió in third-person preterite.

words.es: Consigo los materiales en una tienda del barrio.
words.en: I get the materials at a store in the neighborhood.

words.es: Ayer conseguimos una sala más grande.
words.en: Yesterday we obtained a larger room.

words.es: Ana consiguió hablar con la directora.
words.en: Ana managed to speak with the director.

words.es: ¿Has conseguido el número de la otra oficina?
words.en: Have you obtained the other office's number?

words.es: Espero que consigamos terminar antes del viernes.
words.en: I hope we manage to finish before Friday.

words.es: Si hace falta, pediremos ayuda al grupo de la tarde.
words.en: If necessary, we will ask the afternoon group for help.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing obtaining a result. Conseguir uses consigo / consigues in the present and consiguió in third-person preterite. Conseguir + infinitive can mean manage to do something. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 33. trabajar · Workplaces and collaboration
lessons.objective: 33. trabajar · Workplaces and collaboration: Trabajar en names a workplace or field, de a role, con a collaborator, and para an employer or beneficiary.

words.es: Trabajo en el centro de idiomas.
words.en: I work at the language center.
I used to work as a receptionist.

words.es: Ayer trabajé con el grupo de la mañana.
words.en: Yesterday I worked with the morning group.

words.es: Estamos trabajando para una asociación del barrio.
words.en: We are working for a neighborhood association.

words.es: Si trabajáramos en la misma sala, sería más fácil hablar.
words.en: If we worked in the same room, it would be easier to talk.

words.es: Mañana revisaremos cómo dividir las tareas.
words.en: Tomorrow we will review how to divide the tasks.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing workplaces and collaboration. Trabajar en names a workplace or field, de a role, con a collaborator, and para an employer or beneficiary. It is a regular -ar verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 34. incluir · What a service includes
lessons.objective: 34. incluir · What a service includes: Incluir uses incluyo / incluyes in the present and incluyó / incluyeron in the preterite.

words.es: Incluyo una copia del horario en el mensaje.
words.en: I include a copy of the schedule in the message.

words.es: Ayer incluyeron una fecha nueva en el calendario.
words.en: Yesterday they included a new date in the calendar.
Have they included the person in charge's name?

words.es: Es importante que incluyamos un número de contacto.
words.en: It is important that we include a contact number.

words.es: Así los visitantes podrán avisar si llegan tarde.
words.en: That way visitors will be able to let us know if they arrive late.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing what a service includes. Incluir uses incluyo / incluyes in the present and incluyó / incluyeron in the preterite. Its participle is incluido, without a written accent. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 35. desarrollar · Developing an idea over time
lessons.objective: 35. desarrollar · Developing an idea over time: Desarrollar is regular and commonly means develop a project, idea or skill.
lessons.focus: 35. desarrollar · Developing an idea over time

words.es: Desarrollamos una guía para los nuevos estudiantes.
words.en: We are developing a guide for new students.

words.es: Ana desarrolló la primera propuesta el mes pasado.
words.en: Ana developed the first proposal last month.

words.es: El grupo quiere desarrollar mejores hábitos de estudio.
words.en: The group wants to develop better study habits.

words.es: ¿Podemos desarrollar este ejemplo con más detalle?
words.en: Can we develop this example in more detail?

words.es: La reunión se desarrolló sin problemas.
Al final todos entendimos mejor el objetivo.
words.en: In the end we all understood the objective better.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing developing an idea over time. Desarrollar is regular and commonly means develop a project, idea or skill. Desarrollarse can describe how an event or process unfolds. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 36. hablar · People, topics and an ongoing discussion
lessons.objective: 36. hablar · People, topics and an ongoing discussion: Hablar con names the interlocutor; hablar de or sobre names the topic.
lessons.focus: 36. hablar · People, topics and an ongoing discussion

words.es: Hablo con la coordinadora después de clase.
words.en: I speak with the coordinator after class.

words.es: Hoy hablamos de las nuevas fechas.
words.en: Today we are talking about the new dates.

words.es: Ayer hablé sobre el proyecto con otro grupo.
words.en: Yesterday I spoke about the project with another group.

words.es: ¿Podríamos hablar antes de enviar el mensaje?
words.en: Could we talk before sending the message?

words.es: No quiero hablar por todos sin preguntarles.
words.en: I do not want to speak for everyone without asking them.

words.es: Cada persona puede explicar su situación.
words.en: Each person can explain their situation.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing people, topics and an ongoing discussion. Hablar con names the interlocutor; hablar de or sobre names the topic. Hablar is regular, but its prepositions change the relationship expressed. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 37. salir · Leaving, going out and results
lessons.objective: 37. salir · Leaving, going out and results: Salir de names a starting place; salir a can introduce an activity.
lessons.focus: 37. salir · Leaving, going out and results

words.es: Salgo de la oficina a las cinco.
words.en: I leave the office at five.

words.es: Ayer salimos a buscar otra sala.
words.en: Yesterday we went out to look for another room.

words.es: ¿A qué hora saldrá el próximo autobús?
words.en: What time will the next bus leave?

words.es: No salgas antes de guardar los documentos.
words.en: Do not leave before putting away the documents.

words.es: Cuando terminemos, podremos caminar hasta la estación.
words.en: When we finish, we will be able to walk to the station.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing leaving, going out and results. Salir de names a starting place; salir a can introduce an activity. Salir bien describes a favorable result. Present salgo and future saldré are irregular. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 38. volver · Returning and repeating an action
lessons.objective: 38. volver · Returning and repeating an action: Volver a + infinitive repeats an action; volver a + place returns somewhere.
lessons.focus: 38. volver · Returning and repeating an action

words.es: Vuelvo a la oficina después de comer.
words.en: I return to the office after eating.

words.es: Ayer volvimos a revisar los nombres.
words.en: Yesterday we checked the names again.

words.es: La directora ya ha vuelto de su viaje.
words.en: The director has already returned from her trip.

words.es: ¿Puedes volver a explicar el cambio de sala?
words.en: Can you explain the room change again?

words.es: No quiero que volvamos a perder el mismo mensaje.
words.en: I do not want us to lose the same message again.

words.es: Voy a guardarlo en la carpeta del proyecto.
words.en: I am going to save it in the project folder.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing returning and repeating an action. Volver a + infinitive repeats an action; volver a + place returns somewhere. Present vuelvo and participle vuelto are irregular. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 39. llamar · Calls, names and getting attention
lessons.objective: 39. llamar · Calls, names and getting attention: Llamar a alguien calls a person; llamarse gives a name.
lessons.focus: 39. llamar · Calls, names and getting attention

words.es: Llamo a recepción para confirmar la hora.
words.en: I call reception to confirm the time.

words.es: La nueva coordinadora se llama Isabel.
words.en: The new coordinator is called Isabel.

words.es: Ayer nos llamó cuando llegó la última caja.
words.en: Yesterday she called us when the last box arrived.
Can you call me before leaving?

words.es: El color del aviso llama la atención.
Por eso todos lo vieron al entrar.
words.en: That is why everyone saw it when entering.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing calls, names and getting attention. Llamar a alguien calls a person; llamarse gives a name. Llamar la atención can attract attention or, in context, reprimand someone. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: 40. recibir · Receiving and welcoming
lessons.objective: 40. recibir · Receiving and welcoming: Recibir is a regular -ir verb for receiving something or welcoming someone.

words.es: Recibo las solicitudes por correo electrónico.
Ayer recibimos la confirmación del centro.
words.en: Yesterday we received the center's confirmation.

words.es: Ana va a recibir a los visitantes en la entrada.
words.en: Ana is going to welcome the visitors at the entrance.
Have you received the corrected version?

words.es: Cuando la recibas, comprueba la fecha.
words.en: When you receive it, check the date.

words.es: Después podrás enviarla al resto del grupo.
words.en: Afterward you will be able to send it to the rest of the group.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing receiving and welcoming. Recibir is a regular -ir verb for receiving something or welcoming someone. Receiving a message does not necessarily mean having read or understood it. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

spanish-common-patterns.headline: Spanish Common Grammar Patterns Core 30
spanish-common-patterns.threshold: Use sixty everyday structures, including tener que, hay que, ir a, acabar de and common clause patterns. Ordered for learning, not an asserted statistical frequency ranking.

lessons.title: Acabar de + infinitive
lessons.objective: Acabar de + infinitive: Present acabar de usually describes a very recent completed action; the infinitive does not change.

words.en: I have just cleaned the living room.

words.es: Mi hermano acaba de poner la mesa.
words.en: My brother has just set the table.
Have you just called the visitor?

words.es: Sí, acaba de salir de su casa.
words.en: Yes, she has just left her house.

words.es: Cuando sonó el teléfono, acabábamos de terminar.
words.en: When the phone rang, we had just finished.
Now we can rest for a few minutes.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing just before a visitor arrives. Present acabar de usually describes a very recent completed action; the infinitive does not change. Acababa de locates that recent action before a past point. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Volver a + infinitive
lessons.objective: Volver a + infinitive: Conjugate volver and use a plus infinitive to say do again.

words.es: Voy a volver a leer las instrucciones.
words.en: I am going to read the instructions again.

words.es: Mi compañero volvió a revisar los números.
words.en: My classmate checked the numbers again.

words.es: No queremos volver a cometer el mismo error.
words.en: We do not want to make the same mistake again.

words.es: ¿Puedes volver a explicar el último paso?
words.en: Can you explain the last step again?

words.es: Después volveremos a probar el programa.
words.en: Afterward we will test the program again.

words.es: Esta vez vamos a guardar una copia primero.
words.en: This time we are going to save a copy first.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing retrying a difficult task. Conjugate volver and use a plus infinitive to say do again. Without a second verb, volver often means return to a place. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Empezar a + infinitive
lessons.objective: Empezar a + infinitive: Conjugate empezar and add a before the activity begun.

words.es: Empecé a trabajar en la biblioteca en marzo.
words.en: I started working at the library in March.

words.es: Al principio empezaba a preparar todo muy temprano.
words.en: At first I would start preparing everything very early.

words.es: Ahora empiezo a atender al público a las nueve.
words.en: Now I start serving the public at nine.

words.es: Mi compañera va a empezar a organizar los libros.
words.en: My coworker is going to start organizing the books.

words.es: Antes de abrir, empezamos a revisar las reservas.
words.en: Before opening, we start checking the reservations.
What time do you start resting?

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing the first day of a new routine. Conjugate empezar and add a before the activity begun. Present empiezo and preterite empecé show different changes. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Dejar de + infinitive
lessons.objective: Dejar de + infinitive: Dejar de introduces the activity stopped.

words.es: Dejé de mirar el teléfono antes de dormir.
words.en: I stopped looking at my phone before sleeping.

words.es: Ahora dejo de trabajar a las ocho.
words.en: Now I stop working at eight.

words.es: Mi hermana quiere dejar de tomar café por la noche.
words.en: My sister wants to stop drinking coffee at night.

words.es: No hemos dejado de hablar con nuestros amigos.
words.en: We have not stopped talking to our friends.

words.es: ¿Podrías dejar de hacer ruido un momento?
words.en: Could you stop making noise for a moment?

words.es: Claro, voy a cerrar la puerta con cuidado.
words.en: Of course, I am going to close the door carefully.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing changing an evening habit. Dejar de introduces the activity stopped. Do not confuse it with dejar + infinitive, which can mean let someone do something. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Seguir + gerund
lessons.objective: Seguir + gerund: Seguir + gerund means continue or still be doing something.

words.en: We are still looking for a solution.
Ana is still writing the report.

words.es: El equipo siguió trabajando después del corte de luz.
words.en: The team continued working after the power outage.
Are you going to keep using that file?

words.es: No, pero seguiré guardando las notas en la misma carpeta.
words.en: No, but I will keep saving the notes in the same folder.
If we keep collaborating, we will finish soon.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a project after a setback. Seguir + gerund means continue or still be doing something. Use the gerund, not an infinitive; present sigo / sigues and preterite siguió are irregular. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Estar + gerund
lessons.objective: Estar + gerund: Conjugate estar to locate an action in progress, then use a gerund.

words.es: Mi hermano está cortando las verduras.
words.en: My brother is cutting the vegetables.

words.es: ¿Están usando la receta de la abuela?
Sí, y estamos leyendo cada paso con cuidado.
words.en: Yes, and we are reading each step carefully.

words.es: Cuando llamaste, estaba buscando una olla.
words.en: When you called, I was looking for a pot.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a phone call during dinner. Conjugate estar to locate an action in progress, then use a gerund. It highlights an ongoing action rather than serving as the default for every English -ing form. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Llevar + duration + gerund
lessons.objective: Llevar + duration + gerund: Llevar plus a duration and gerund expresses an activity continuing for that length of time; present Spanish often corresponds to English have been doing.

words.es: Llevo una hora esperando una respuesta.
words.en: I have been waiting for an answer for an hour.

words.es: Mi compañera lleva dos días revisando el documento.
words.en: My coworker has been reviewing the document for two days.
How long have you been working together?

words.es: Llevamos seis meses preparando el proyecto.
words.en: We have been preparing the project for six months.

words.es: Ayer ya llevaba varios minutos buscando el mensaje.
words.en: Yesterday I had already been looking for the message for several minutes.
We hope to finish this week.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing waiting for a decision. Llevar plus a duration and gerund expresses an activity continuing for that length of time; present Spanish often corresponds to English have been doing. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Terminar de + infinitive
lessons.objective: Terminar de + infinitive: Terminar de introduces the activity completed.

words.es: Terminé de ordenar las mesas a las seis.
words.en: I finished arranging the tables at six.

words.es: Mi compañera terminó de contar los libros.
words.en: My coworker finished counting the books.
Have you finished writing the notice?

words.es: Todavía no; voy a terminar de revisarlo primero.
words.en: Not yet; I am going to finish checking it first.

words.es: Cuando terminemos de limpiar, podremos salir.
words.en: When we finish cleaning, we will be able to leave.

words.es: No cierres antes de terminar de guardar las llaves.
words.en: Do not close before finishing putting the keys away.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing closing the library. Terminar de introduces the activity completed. Conjugate terminar; the second verb stays in the infinitive. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Tratar de + infinitive
lessons.objective: Tratar de + infinitive: Tratar de expresses an attempt: trato de entender.

words.es: Trato de entender la última frase.
words.en: I am trying to understand the last sentence.

words.es: Mi amiga trató de llamar al autor.
words.en: My friend tried to call the author.

words.es: Estamos tratando de encontrar un ejemplo más claro.
words.en: We are trying to find a clearer example.

words.es: No trates de adivinar todos los detalles.
words.en: Do not try to guess all the details.

words.es: Primero trata de reconocer la idea principal.
words.en: First try to recognize the main idea.

words.es: Después podemos comprobar las palabras nuevas.
words.en: Afterward we can check the new words.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing understanding a difficult message. Tratar de expresses an attempt: trato de entender. Tratar a alguien concerns treatment of a person; tratar de un tema concerns a subject. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Tener ganas de + infinitive
lessons.objective: Tener ganas de + infinitive: Tener ganas de means feel like doing something.

words.es: Tengo ganas de salir a caminar.
words.en: I feel like going out for a walk.
Do you feel like coming with me?

words.es: Hoy no tengo ganas de ir muy lejos.
words.en: Today I do not feel like going very far.

words.es: Mis amigos tenían ganas de conocer el parque.
words.en: My friends felt like getting to know the park.

words.es: Podemos descansar allí si tenemos ganas de sentarnos.
words.en: We can rest there if we feel like sitting down.

words.es: Al final todos tenemos ganas de tomar algo caliente.
words.en: In the end we all feel like having something hot to drink.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing an invitation after class. Tener ganas de means feel like doing something. Ganas stays plural; conjugate tener and retain de before the infinitive. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Tener tiempo para + infinitive
lessons.objective: Tener tiempo para + infinitive: Tener tiempo para states time available for an activity.

words.es: Tengo tiempo para estudiar antes de cenar.
words.en: I have time to study before dinner.
Do you have time to review my notes?

words.es: Ayer no tuvimos tiempo para terminar.
words.en: Yesterday we did not have time to finish.

words.es: Mañana tendré tiempo para llamar al profesor.
words.en: Tomorrow I will have time to call the teacher.

words.es: Si organizamos la tarde, tendremos tiempo para descansar.
words.en: If we organize the afternoon, we will have time to rest.

words.es: No hace falta hacer todo de una vez.
words.en: There is no need to do everything at once.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing finding a study slot. Tener tiempo para states time available for an activity. Do not confuse para with the de in tener ganas de. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Estar a punto de + infinitive
lessons.objective: Estar a punto de + infinitive: Estar a punto de describes an action on the verge of happening.

words.es: Estaba a punto de salir cuando llamó mi madre.
words.en: I was about to leave when my mother called.

words.es: Ella estaba a punto de subir al tren.
words.en: She was about to board the train.

words.es: Estamos a punto de terminar la conversación.
words.en: We are about to finish the conversation.

words.es: ¿Estás a punto de perder la conexión?
words.en: Are you about to lose the connection?

words.es: Sí, el tren está a punto de entrar en un túnel.
words.en: Yes, the train is about to enter a tunnel.
Then I will call you when you arrive.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing almost missing a call. Estar a punto de describes an action on the verge of happening. In the past it can describe an event that nearly occurred without asserting it happened. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Estar de acuerdo con
lessons.objective: Estar de acuerdo con: Estar de acuerdo expresses agreement; con names the person or proposal.

words.es: Estoy de acuerdo con la propuesta de Ana.
No todos están de acuerdo con el horario.
words.en: Not everyone agrees with the schedule.

words.es: Estamos de acuerdo en reunirnos el jueves.
words.en: We agree to meet on Thursday.

words.es: ¿Estás de acuerdo con cambiar de sala?
words.en: Do you agree with changing rooms?

words.es: Sí, pero no estoy de acuerdo con empezar más tarde.
words.en: Yes, but I do not agree with starting later.

words.es: Busquemos una opción que funcione para todos.
words.en: Let us look for an option that works for everyone.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing agreeing on a meeting plan. Estar de acuerdo expresses agreement; con names the person or proposal. For an action use estar de acuerdo en + infinitive where appropriate. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Hay + noun: existence
lessons.objective: Hay + noun: existence: Hay introduces existence and does not agree with a plural noun.

words.es: Hay diez sillas en el aula.
words.en: There are ten chairs in the classroom.

words.es: También hay una mesa junto a la ventana.
words.en: There is also a table next to the window.
Is there enough space for the group?

words.es: Sí, pero no hay ningún proyector.
words.en: Yes, but there is no projector.

words.es: El proyector está en la sala de al lado.
words.en: The projector is in the room next door.

words.es: Había dos aquí el año pasado.
words.en: There were two here last year.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing checking a classroom. Hay introduces existence and does not agree with a plural noun. To locate an already identified thing, commonly use estar. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Hace tiempo que + present
lessons.objective: Hace tiempo que + present: Hace + duration + que with an ongoing present situation expresses how long it has continued.

words.es: Hace tiempo que estudio en este centro.
words.en: I have been studying at this center for a while.

words.es: Hace dos años que trabajo cerca de aquí.
words.en: I have worked near here for two years.

words.es: ¿Hace cuánto tiempo que vives en el barrio?
words.en: How long have you lived in the neighborhood?

words.es: Hace seis meses que vivo junto al parque.
words.en: I have lived next to the park for six months.

words.es: Hace mucho que no veo a nuestros antiguos compañeros.
words.en: I have not seen our old classmates for a long time.

words.es: Podríamos invitarlos a tomar un café.
words.en: We could invite them for a coffee.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing catching up with a friend. Hace + duration + que with an ongoing present situation expresses how long it has continued. Negation can describe how long an event has not happened. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Desde hace + duration
lessons.objective: Desde hace + duration: Desde hace names elapsed duration continuing to a reference point, commonly with present for an ongoing situation.

words.es: Trabajo aquí desde hace tres semanas.
words.en: I have worked here for three weeks.

words.es: Mi hermana estudia español desde hace un año.
words.en: My sister has studied Spanish for a year.

words.es: Desde hace dos días no funciona el ascensor.
words.en: The elevator has not worked for two days.
How long have you been waiting?
I have been waiting for half an hour.

words.es: Si no llega pronto, volveré mañana.
words.en: If he does not arrive soon, I will return tomorrow.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing describing a new routine. Desde hace names elapsed duration continuing to a reference point, commonly with present for an ongoing situation. Desde alone can name a starting date. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Hace + duration: ago
lessons.objective: Hace + duration: ago: Hace + duration with a bounded past event means ago.

words.es: Llegué a esta ciudad hace tres meses.
words.en: I arrived in this city three months ago.

words.es: Conocí a mis vecinos hace dos semanas.
words.en: I met my neighbors two weeks ago.

words.es: Hace unos días cambié de horario.
words.en: A few days ago I changed my schedule.
How long ago did you start the course?
I started it a month ago.

words.es: Desde entonces practico un poco cada día.
words.en: Since then I practice a little every day.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing explaining when things changed. Hace + duration with a bounded past event means ago. Contrast it with an ongoing present situation using hace ... que or desde hace. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Tardar en + infinitive
lessons.objective: Tardar en + infinitive: Tardar plus a duration and en + infinitive states the time an action takes.

words.es: Tardo veinte minutos en llegar al trabajo.
words.en: It takes me twenty minutes to get to work.

words.es: El autobús tarda más en llegar cuando llueve.
words.en: The bus takes longer to arrive when it rains.

words.es: Ayer tardé casi una hora en volver.
words.en: Yesterday it took me almost an hour to return.

words.es: ¿Cuánto tardas en caminar hasta la estación?
words.en: How long does it take you to walk to the station?

words.es: Tardo diez minutos en llegar allí.
words.en: It takes me ten minutes to get there.
Tomorrow I will compare the two routes.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing comparing two routes. Tardar plus a duration and en + infinitive states the time an action takes. The subject may be a person, service or process. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Quedar en + infinitive
lessons.objective: Quedar en + infinitive: Quedar en introduces an agreement about what to do.

words.es: Quedamos en llamar a Marta después de clase.
words.en: We agreed to call Marta after class.

words.es: Ella quedó en enviar los documentos hoy.
words.en: She agreed to send the documents today.

words.es: ¿Habíamos quedado en revisar también el precio?
words.en: Had we agreed to review the price too?

words.es: Sí, pero primero quedamos en confirmar la fecha.
words.en: Yes, but first we agreed to confirm the date.

words.es: No recuerdo si quedamos en reunirnos aquí.
words.en: I do not remember whether we agreed to meet here.

words.es: Voy a comprobar el mensaje antes de salir.
words.en: I am going to check the message before leaving.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing confirming a shared task. Quedar en introduces an agreement about what to do. Quedar a + time and quedar con + person serve different roles. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Quedarse sin + noun / infinitive
lessons.objective: Quedarse sin + noun / infinitive: Quedarse sin describes being left without something; with an infinitive it can describe something left undone.

words.es: Me quedé sin batería durante el viaje.
words.en: I ran out of battery during the journey.

words.es: Mi hermana se quedó sin conexión.
Nos quedamos sin poder abrir la reserva.
words.en: We were left unable to open the reservation.

words.es: No quiero quedarme sin dinero en efectivo.
words.en: I do not want to be left without cash.

words.es: Por suerte no nos quedamos sin boletos.
words.en: Fortunately we were not left without tickets.

words.es: La próxima vez llevaré una copia en papel.
words.en: Next time I will bring a paper copy.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a journey without a charger. Quedarse sin describes being left without something; with an infinitive it can describe something left undone. Match the reflexive pronoun to the subject. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Ser necesario + infinitive
lessons.objective: Ser necesario + infinitive: Es necesario plus infinitive makes a general statement.

words.en: It is necessary to complete this form.

words.es: También es necesario mostrar una identificación.
words.en: It is also necessary to show identification.
Is it necessary to bring a photo?
It is not necessary to pay today.

words.es: Para reservar la plaza, es necesario confirmar el horario.
words.en: To reserve the place, it is necessary to confirm the schedule.

words.es: Después podemos elegir el grupo que más nos convenga.
words.en: Afterward we can choose the group that suits us best.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing before registering for a course. Es necesario plus infinitive makes a general statement. With a specific new subject, es necesario que normally takes subjunctive. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Es importante que + subjunctive
lessons.objective: Es importante que + subjunctive: A judgment such as es importante que normally takes subjunctive for the action evaluated; the verb reflects the subject after que.

words.es: Es importante que practiques con tiempo.
words.en: It is important that you practice ahead of time.

words.es: También es importante que todos entiendan el objetivo.
words.en: It is also important that everyone understand the objective.

words.es: Es importante que no leas cada palabra.
words.en: It is important that you not read every word.
Is it important that we bring pictures?

words.es: Sí, pero es más importante que sean claras.
words.en: Yes, but it is more important that they be clear.

words.es: Podemos revisar juntos el primer ejemplo.
words.en: We can review the first example together.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing preparing an oral presentation. A judgment such as es importante que normally takes subjunctive for the action evaluated; the verb reflects the subject after que. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Es mejor que + subjunctive
lessons.objective: Es mejor que + subjunctive: Es mejor que recommends an action with a specified subject, normally using subjunctive.

words.es: Es mejor que cierres la puerta durante la grabación.
words.en: It is better if you close the door during the recording.

words.es: También es mejor que apagues el ventilador.
words.en: It is also better if you turn off the fan.
Is it better if we use another microphone?

words.es: Creo que es mejor probar primero.
words.en: I think it is better to test first.

words.es: Es mejor que no cambien todo al mismo tiempo.
words.en: It is better if they do not change everything at the same time.
That way we will know which change helps.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing advice about a noisy room. Es mejor que recommends an action with a specified subject, normally using subjunctive. Es mejor + infinitive can give advice without a new explicit subject. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Esperar que + subjunctive
lessons.objective: Esperar que + subjunctive: Esperar que expresses a hope with subjunctive.

words.es: Espero que mis padres lleguen temprano.
words.en: I hope my parents arrive early.

words.es: Esperamos que el tren no se retrase.
words.en: We hope the train is not delayed.

words.es: Mi madre espera que podamos cenar juntos.
words.en: My mother hopes we can have dinner together.

words.es: Yo espero terminar el trabajo antes de las seis.
words.en: I hope to finish work before six.

words.es: También espero que les guste la ciudad.
words.en: I also hope they like the city.
When they arrive, we will go for a walk.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing hoping a visit goes well. Esperar que expresses a hope with subjunctive. Esperar + infinitive can keep the same subject; esperar also means wait in other constructions. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Querer que + subjunctive
lessons.objective: Querer que + subjunctive: Querer que introduces a wanted action by a different subject and normally takes subjunctive.

words.es: Quiero que ayudemos a nuestra vecina.
words.en: I want us to help our neighbor.

words.es: Ella quiere que llevemos las bolsas hasta la cocina.
words.en: She wants us to carry the bags to the kitchen.

words.es: No quiere que movamos la mesa.
words.en: She does not want us to move the table.

words.es: Mi hermano quiere ayudar con las plantas.
words.en: My brother wants to help with the plants.

words.es: Yo quiero que todos sepamos qué hacer.
words.en: I want all of us to know what to do.

words.es: Primero vamos a preguntarle qué necesita.
words.en: First we are going to ask her what she needs.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing organizing help for a neighbor. Querer que introduces a wanted action by a different subject and normally takes subjunctive. Compare quiero ayudar with quiero que ayudes. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: No creo que + subjunctive
lessons.objective: No creo que + subjunctive: No creo que commonly presents a belief as rejected or uncertain and takes subjunctive.

words.es: No creo que ese anuncio sea reciente.
words.en: I do not think that notice is recent.

words.es: Tampoco creo que el centro cierre los sábados.
words.en: I do not think the center closes on Saturdays either.

words.es: Mi amiga cree que hay otro horario en la entrada.
words.en: My friend thinks there is another schedule at the entrance.

words.es: No creo que debamos cambiar el plan todavía.
words.en: I do not think we should change the plan yet.

words.es: Es mejor que confirmemos la información.
words.en: It is better if we confirm the information.

words.es: Voy a llamar antes de enviar el mensaje al grupo.
words.en: I am going to call before sending the message to the group.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing checking a doubtful announcement. No creo que commonly presents a belief as rejected or uncertain and takes subjunctive. Creo que normally introduces indicative. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Parece que + indicative
lessons.objective: Parece que + indicative: Parece que normally reports an impression using indicative; it does not automatically trigger subjunctive.

words.es: Parece que el tren va a salir de otra vía.
words.en: It seems the train is going to leave from another track.

words.es: Me parece que han cambiado el anuncio.
words.en: It seems to me that they have changed the announcement.

words.es: El empleado dice que la vía anterior está cerrada.
words.en: The employee says the previous track is closed.

words.es: Parecía que todos sabían adónde ir.
words.en: It seemed everyone knew where to go.

words.es: No parece que tengamos mucho tiempo.
words.en: It does not seem that we have much time.

words.es: Vamos a preguntar antes de mover las maletas.
words.en: Let us ask before moving the suitcases.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing noticing a change at a station. Parece que normally reports an impression using indicative; it does not automatically trigger subjunctive. Me parece que marks an opinion. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Decir que: reporting information
lessons.objective: Decir que: reporting information: Decir que can report a statement with indicative.

words.es: Ana dice que la reunión será en otra sala.
words.en: Ana says the meeting will be in another room.

words.es: El director dijo que la sala anterior estaba ocupada.
words.en: The director said the previous room was occupied.

words.es: También dijo que enviaría un mapa.
words.en: He also said he would send a map.

words.es: Yo les dije a mis compañeros que podía acompañarlos.
words.en: I told my coworkers that I could go with them.

words.es: No dije que la reunión estuviera cancelada.
words.en: I did not say the meeting was canceled.

words.es: Ahora voy a reenviar el mensaje completo.
words.en: Now I am going to forward the complete message.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing passing on a change of room. Decir que can report a statement with indicative. Distinguish reported facts from telling someone to do something, which can require subjunctive. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

lessons.title: Pedir que + subjunctive
lessons.objective: Pedir que + subjunctive: Pedir que introduces a requested action, normally with subjunctive.

words.es: Te pido que revises la fecha del documento.
words.en: I ask you to check the date on the document.

words.es: La coordinadora nos pide que usemos la versión nueva.
words.en: The coordinator asks us to use the new version.

words.es: Ayer pidió que no enviáramos la copia antigua.
words.en: Yesterday she asked us not to send the old copy.

words.es: También me pidió que confirmara los nombres.
words.en: She also asked me to confirm the names.

words.es: No te pido que hagas todo solo.
